short: A permanent price cut used to clear stock that is not moving.
metaDescription: A markdown is a permanent reduction in an item's selling price, usually to clear slow-moving, seasonal or near-expiry stock.
definition: A markdown is a permanent reduction in an item's selling price, usually to clear slow-moving, seasonal or near-expiry stock. Unlike a promotional discount, the price does not go back up.
bodyHtml:
Why Markdown matters

Markdowns recover cash from stock that would otherwise become dead. Taken early they cost a little margin; delayed until the goods are unsellable, they cost the entire purchase.

Markdown formula

Markdown % = (Original price − New price) ÷ Original price × 100

Cumulative markdowns should be measured against the original price, not the last reduced one.

How Markdown works in practice

Set an ageing rule per category — for instance, review anything unsold after 60 days — and mark down in steps rather than waiting for a clearance event. Record the markdown so the margin report reflects reality.

faq.question: When should I mark stock down?
faq.answer: As soon as the ageing report says it will not sell at full price. Waiting reduces what the goods can still fetch.

faq.question: How is markdown different from discount?
faq.answer: A markdown resets the price permanently; a discount is a temporary reduction from a price that remains in force.
